issues.description: Public API quietly demoted to package-private without a deprecation cycle
issues.detail: NAME, QUANTIZED_VECTOR_COMPONENT, calculateDefaultConfidenceInterval, OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues.load, the SparseOffHeapVectorValues ctor, and the reader class all flip from public to package-private in the same patch that moves packages. Anything downstream that imported these — and people do, this is Lucene — gets a hard compile break with no @Deprecated grace period. Either keep them public in the new package or land the visibility change as a separate, announced patch.

issues.description: THREE-PATCHES: package move, visibility shrink, and writer-disable are one commit
issues.detail: This diff does at least three independent things: (1) physically relocate classes to backward_codecs, (2) tighten visibility on a half-dozen symbols, (3) replace working fieldsWriter implementations with UnsupportedOperationException. When something regresses, bisect lands on a blob. Split: move first (mechanical, reviewable at a glance), then disable writes, then tighten visibility — each justifiable on its own.

issues.description: @Deprecated annotation dropped while removing the writer — wrong signal direction
issues.detail: Both formats lose @Deprecated in this patch. A read-only legacy codec that throws on write is *more* deprecated than before, not less. Users on the old format need the compiler warning to know they must migrate before the next major. Keep @Deprecated, ideally with forRemoval and a since= pointing at the replacement Lucene104 format.

issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException with no migration pointer
issues.detail: "Old codecs may only be used for reading" tells the user nothing actionable. The exception message should name the replacement (Lucene104HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat) so the stack trace is the migration doc. Cheap fix, high payoff — this is the error someone will hit at 2am on a rolling upgrade.

issues.description: PR description admits the job is half-done — Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorScorer still in core
issues.detail: Author says they couldn't move Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorScorer "just yet." That means core still depends on lucene99 quantization machinery while the format pretending to own it lives in backward_codecs. This is the kind of split-brain that bites maintainers six months later. Acceptable as an interim, but the follow-up patch needs to exist as a tracked issue, not a TODO in a PR description.

issues.description: protected fields downgraded to package-private on a public abstract class
issues.detail: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues is public abstract; its fields go from protected to package-private. Any subclass outside this package — which is the whole point of `protected` on an abstract class — now can't see them. If no external subclass exists, fine; if one does, this is a silent break. Worth a one-line justification in the commit message or revert to protected.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The package move itself is mechanical and fine, and disabling writes on a legacy format is the right shape. But this patch is doing three things at once — relocate, shrink visibility, kill the writer — and that makes it hostile to bisect and hostile to downstream consumers who lose public symbols with no deprecation cycle. The dropped @Deprecated annotation actively misleads users in the wrong direction, and the UnsupportedOperationException message refuses to name the replacement format. Split into separate patches, restore @Deprecated, make the throw message point at Lucene104, and either keep the API surface public in the new package or announce the visibility tightening on its own.
